words.tr: adv. 幼稚地; 天真地，幼小地
words.ex: He behaved childishly when he refused to share his toys.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝分享他的玩具，表现得非常幼稚。
words.en: In a manner that is characteristic of a child; immaturely or naively.

words.ex: She insists on going home now.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决要求现在回家。
words.en: If you insist on doing something, you keep doing it, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr: adj. 国家主义的；民族主义的
words.ex: His nationalistic views often led to conflict with other political factions.
words.ex_cn: 他的民族主义观点常常与其他政治派别发生冲突。
words.en: If you describe someone as nationalistic, you mean they are very proud of their nation. They also often believe that their nation is better than any other nation, and in this case, you can describe them as chauvinistic nationalistic.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.tr: phrase. 跳远（田径项目中的一种跳跃比赛，即立定跳远或助跑跳远）
words.ex: He practiced the broad jump every day to improve his athletic performance.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习跳远以提高运动表现。
words.en: A track and field event in which competitors jump as far as possible from a standing start or a short run.

words.ex: He is a sophomore at Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的二年级学生。
words.en: A sophomore is a student in the second year of college or high school.

words.ex: I expect a gift on my birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我期待在生日时收到一份礼物。
words.en: If you expect something, you believe that it is likely to happen or that it will be the case.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.ex: The dog fell into a deep pit.
words.ex_cn: 狗掉进了一个深坑。
words.en: A pit is a large hole in the ground, either natural or as a result of digging. It can also refer to a hollow or indentation in a surface, or a place where something is extracted, such as a mine. As a verb, to pit means to set someone or something in competition or to make a hollow or indentation in a surface.

words.tr: phrase. 结果是；原来是；证实是
words.ex: The shy boy turned out to be a great singer.
words.ex_cn: 那个害羞的男孩结果是个很棒的歌手。
words.en: If something turns out to be a particular thing, it is discovered to be that thing.

words.ex: Everyone passed the test, with one exception.
words.ex_cn: 所有人都通过了考试，只有一个例外。
words.en: An exception is a person or thing that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: The plane's takeoff was delayed by strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 飞机的起飞因强风而延误了。
words.en: Takeoff is the beginning of a flight, when an aircraft leaves the ground.

words.tr:
n. 板；董事会；
v. 上船（或火车、飞机等）；
words.ex: He nailed the picture to the board.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片钉在板上。
words.en: A board is a flat, thin, rectangular piece of wood or other material used for a particular purpose, such as cutting food on or as a surface for writing or playing games. It can also refer to a group of people who manage or control a company or organization, or to the meals provided by an institution such as a school or hospital. As a verb, it means to get onto a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle, or to provide meals and lodging for someone.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: He kick the ball into the goal.
words.ex_cn: 他把球踢进了球门。
words.en: To strike or propel with the foot; a blow or thrust delivered by the foot.

words.ex: She looked at the mess disgustedly and left the room.
words.ex_cn: 她厌烦地看着那片混乱，然后离开了房间。
words.en: In a manner that shows strong disapproval or distaste.

words.ex: He washed his hands to remove the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他洗手以去除污垢。
words.en: Dirt is any substance that makes something unclean, such as mud or dust.

words.ex: He gave the rope a twist to tie it tight.
words.ex_cn: 他把绳子拧了一下以便系紧。
words.en: To twist something means to turn it in a different direction or to change its shape by turning it.

words.ex: He uses a lot of slang when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时用很多俚语。
words.en: Slang refers to a type of language that consists of words and phrases that are regarded as very informal, are more common in speech than writing, and are typically restricted to a particular context or group of people.

words.tr: phrase. 下苦功；费心尽力；认真努力做某事
words.ex: He takes pains to help his classmates with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他费尽心思帮助同学做作业。
words.en: If you take pains to do something or go to great pains to do something, you try hard to do it, because you think it is important to do it.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.ex: After the break, we will proceed with the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 休息后，我们将继续开会。
words.en: If you proceed to do something, you continue to do it or start to do it after doing something else first.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.tr: phrase. 在那一瞬间；就在那时
words.ex: She realized the truth at the instant she saw his face.
words.ex_cn: 她在看到他的脸的瞬间意识到了真相。
words.en: At the very moment something happens.

words.ex: He glares at the boy because the boy took his pencil.
words.ex_cn: 他怒视那个男孩，因为男孩拿了他的铅笔。
words.en: To look at someone or something in an angry way.

words.tr:
v. 站立；忍受；
n. 立足点；
words.ex: The boy stands near the door.
words.ex_cn: 男孩站在门附近。
words.en: If you stand somewhere, you are in an upright position with your feet on the ground. If something stands somewhere, it is in an upright position in that place.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.tr:
n. 紧握；掌握；控制；
v. 紧握；掌握；
words.ex: He has a strong grip on the handle.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握住把手。
words.en: To grip something means to hold it tightly. It can also mean to hold someone's attention completely.

words.tr: n. 电镀；镀层; v. 电镀（plate 的现在分词）
words.ex: The plating on the metal started to peel off.
words.ex_cn: 金属上的镀层开始剥落。
words.en: Plating is the process of covering a metal object with a thin layer of another metal, especially by electrolysis.

words.tr: n. 克拉（宝石重量单位）；开（含纯金的量）
words.ex: The diamond weighs two carats.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石重两克拉。
words.en: A unit of weight for precious stones and pearls, equivalent to 200 milligrams.

words.ex: He was busy at the moment.
words.ex_cn: 当时他很忙。
words.en: At the moment is used to indicate that something is happening now.

words.tr: 短语动词，意思是心里有某个想法、计划或偏好；心中已有打算
words.ex: I have something in mind for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我脑子里有个晚餐的想法。
words.en: To be thinking of a particular plan or idea.

words.tr: phrase. 心里想着某人；有意让某人做某事
words.ex: I have a specific person in mind for this job.
words.ex_cn: 我心里有一个人选适合这份工作。
words.en: To consider someone for a particular role or purpose.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.tr: adj. 专门的；专业的； v. “specialize”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He has a specialized job in computer repair.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作是专门修理电脑的。
words.en: Requiring or involving detailed and specific knowledge or training.

words.ex: He shifted the gear to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他换挡以减慢车速。
words.en: Gear refers to a toothed wheel that works with others to alter the relation between the speed of a driving mechanism (such as the engine of a vehicle) and the speed of the driven parts (the wheels). It can also mean equipment that is used for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr: v. 参加风帆冲浪运动
words.ex: He windsurfs on the lake every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都在湖上玩风帆冲浪。
words.en: To engage in the sport of riding on water on a sailboard.

words.tr: phrase. 激流泛舟；在湍急白浪中乘橡皮筏漂流的运动
words.ex: They went white-water rafting on the river last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周末去河上进行激流筏艇。
words.en: The activity of travelling down a river on a raft, especially on rivers where the current is very fast and the water is very rough.

words.ex: The river has dangerous rapids near the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在岩石附近有危险的急流。
words.en: Rapids are a section of a river where the water moves very fast, often over rocks.

words.tr: phrase. & n. 蹦极跳；一种从高处跃下并由弹性绳索系住脚踝的极限运动
words.ex: She decided to try bungee jumping for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 她决定第一次尝试蹦极跳。
words.en: An activity in which a person jumps from a high place (such as a bridge) while attached to an elastic cord.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.ex: The boy rides his skateboard to school.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩骑着他的滑板去学校。
words.en: A skateboard is a narrow board with wheels on the bottom that you stand on and ride as a sport or for fun.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.tr: phrase. 天空冲浪（一种极限运动，运动员在跳伞时脚踩冲浪板在空中做特技动作）
words.ex: He tried sky surfing for the first time and found it exhilarating.
words.ex_cn: 他第一次尝试空中冲浪，感到非常兴奋。
words.en: Sky surfing is an extreme sport in which the surfer jumps from an airplane and uses a surfboard to glide through the air.

words.ex: The contestant won the singing competition.
words.ex_cn: 这位竞争者赢得了歌唱比赛。
words.en: A contestant is someone who takes part in a competition or contest.

words.tr: adj. 袋状的；宽松的；松弛垂落的
words.ex: He wears baggy jeans to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿宽松的牛仔裤去参加派对。
words.en: If a piece of clothing is baggy, it hangs loosely on your body.

words.ex: He likes to study philosophy in his free time.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在空闲时间学习哲学。
words.en: Philosophy is the study or creation of theories about basic things such as the nature of existence, knowledge, and thought, or about how people should live.

words.tr:
adj. 蛮勇的；鲁莽大胆的
n. 鲁莽大胆的人
words.ex: He is a daredevil rider who jumps over cars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个蛮勇的骑手，会跳过汽车。
words.en: A daredevil is someone who enjoys doing dangerous things and taking risks.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: n. 娱乐；消遣；休闲活动
words.ex: Reading books is his favorite recreation.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: Recreation is activity that you do for enjoyment or amusement when you are not working.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.tr: phrase. 诺贝尔奖；为表彰在物理、化学、生理学或医学、文学、和平及经济学领域作出杰出贡献者而设立的国际奖项
words.ex: He won the Nobel Prize for physics.
words.ex_cn: 他因物理学获得了诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The Nobel Prize is a set of annual international awards bestowed in several categories by Swedish and Norwegian institutions in recognition of academic, cultural, or scientific advances.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.ex: He felt proud of his academic achievement.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的学业成就感到自豪。
words.en: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He studies physiology to understand how the human body works.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生理学以了解人体如何运作。
words.en: The branch of biology that deals with the normal functions of living organisms and their parts.

words.ex: His headaches are linked to too much screen time.
words.ex_cn: 他的头痛与过多的屏幕时间有关。
words.en: To be connected or associated with something or someone.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.tr: phrase. 诺贝尔基金会（负责管理诺贝尔奖相关事务的瑞典机构）
words.ex: The Nobel Foundation was established in 1900 to manage the assets made available through the will of Alfred Nobel.
words.ex_cn: 诺贝尔基金会成立于1900年，负责管理阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔遗嘱中提供的资产。
words.en: The Nobel Foundation is a private institution founded in 1900 based on the will of Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite. It is responsible for the final selection of the Nobel Prize winners and the management of the Nobel assets.

words.tr:
auxv. 将会；愿意；
n. 意志；意愿；遗嘱；
words.ex: I will go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天会去公园。
words.en: The word 'will' can be used as a noun to refer to the faculty by which a person decides on and initiates action, or as a verb to indicate a desire or intention to do something.

words.ex: The establishment of the school took five years.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的建立花了五年时间。
words.en: The act of establishing something or the state of being established. It can also refer to an organization or institution, especially a business or public body.

words.ex: He starts with math problems every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上从数学题开始。
words.en: To begin with or include something as a preliminary part or element.

words.tr: 短语动词，表示‘称某人为某物’，例如：They call him Tom.（他们称他为汤姆。）
words.ex: He likes to call his sister 'princess'.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢称呼他的妹妹为“公主”。
words.en: To give someone or something a particular name or title.

words.ex: He trades in old cars for new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧车换新车。
words.en: To exchange a used item as part of the payment for a new one.

words.tr:
adj. 爆炸的；
n. 炸药；
words.ex: The explosive material was handled with care.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸性材料被小心地处理。
words.en: An explosive substance is capable of causing an explosion. It can also refer to something that is likely to cause an outburst or a sudden increase in activity or emotion.

words.tr: phrase. 放下；记下；镇压；贬低；削减；杀死
words.ex: He put down his pen and smiled.
words.ex_cn: 他放下笔，笑了。
words.en: To place something on a surface or in a particular position; to write something down; to suppress or end something by force; to criticize someone in a way that makes them seem stupid or unimportant.

words.ex: He made a mistake in his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在作业中犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you make a mistake, you do something which you did not intend to do, or which produces a result that you do not want.

words.tr: phrase. 尽管如此；仍然；还是
words.ex: He didn't study, but all the same, he passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有学习，但尽管如此，他还是通过了考试。
words.en: Despite that; nevertheless.

words.ex: He spends time reading books every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天花时间读书。
words.en: To use time to do a particular activity or task.

words.ex: He creates beautiful paintings with colors.
words.ex_cn: 他用色彩创造美丽的画作。
words.en: To create means to bring something into existence or to cause something to happen as a result of one's actions.

words.ex: He invented a new machine to clean the house.
words.ex_cn: 他发明了一台新机器来打扫房子。
words.en: To invent something means to design or create it, especially something that has never been made before.

words.ex: He found a weapon in the old box.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧箱子里发现了一件武器。
words.en: A weapon is an object that can be used to harm or kill someone, or to damage or destroy something.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 某人那个时代（最杰出、最有名或最典型）的
words.ex: He was the best basketball player of his day.
words.ex_cn: 他是他那个时代最好的篮球运动员。
words.en: Belonging to a particular person's time or era; the peak period of someone's life or career.

words.ex: Polar bears live near the north pole.
words.ex_cn: 北极熊生活在北极附近。
words.en: The North Pole is the northernmost point on the Earth, lying diametrically opposite the South Pole.

words.ex: He finished his homework at last.
words.ex_cn: 他终于完成了作业。
words.en: After a long time or delay; finally.

words.tr: phrase. 与...相处；忍受；处理；与…有关；需要；想做
words.ex: I don't know how to do with him; he is always quiet.
words.ex_cn: 我不知道怎么和他相处；他总是很安静。
words.en: To have a connection or relevance to a particular subject or situation.

words.tr:
n. 荣誉；荣幸；尊敬；
v. 尊敬；给予荣誉；履行；
words.ex: He received an honor for his brave actions.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢的行为获得了荣誉。
words.en: Honor is a quality that combines respect, pride, and honesty. A person who has honor is someone who is admired and respected because of his or her integrity and ethical behavior.

words.tr:
v. 想知道；
n. 惊奇；奇迹；
words.ex: I wonder why he is late.
words.ex_cn: 我想知道他为什么迟到了。
words.en: To feel curiosity or doubt about something; a feeling of surprise mingled with admiration, caused by something beautiful, unexpected, unfamiliar, or inexplicable.

words.ex: I just learned of the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我刚刚得知明天的会议。
words.en: To become aware of something, typically by being told about it.

words.ex: He works in the field of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机科学领域工作。
words.en: In the field of refers to being involved in a particular area of study or activity.

words.ex: He majors in economics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修经济学。
words.en: Economics is the study of the way in which money, industry, and trade are organized in a society.

words.ex: He didn't study hard, as a result, he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有努力学习，结果考试不及格。
words.en: used to introduce the consequence or effect of a particular situation or event

words.ex: She loves Swedish meatballs.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢瑞典肉丸。
words.en: Of, relating to, or characteristic of Sweden, its people, or their language.

words.tr: n. 加州理工学院（California Institute of Technology）
words.ex: He got accepted to Caltech for engineering.
words.ex_cn: 他被加州理工学院录取学工程。
words.en: California Institute of Technology, a private research university located in Pasadena, California, known for its strength in science and engineering.

words.tr:
v. 作嗡嗡声；飞驰；陡升
n. 直线上升；激增；嗡嗡声
words.ex: The bee zooms around the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在花丛中嗡嗡飞舞。
words.en: to move quickly or suddenly with a loud, low, continuous noise, or to make something do this

words.ex: The storm caused a disruption in the phone line.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨导致电话线路中断。
words.en: A phone line is a physical line or circuit that connects a telephone to a telecommunications network.

words.tr:
adj. 埃及的；
n. 埃及语；
words.ex: She bought an Egyptian scarf at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一条埃及风格的围巾。
words.en: Of or relating to Egypt or its people, language, or culture.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: His reaction was quick when the ball came at him.
words.ex_cn: 当球朝他飞来时，他的反应很快。
words.en: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.

words.tr: phrase. 那又怎样；有什么了不起（用于表示不关心或轻蔑）
words.ex: So what if it's raining? We can still go out.
words.ex_cn: 那又怎样，下雨了？我们仍然可以出去。
words.en: An expression used to dismiss something as unimportant or to challenge the significance of a statement.

words.ex: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awards the Nobel Prize in Physics.
words.ex_cn: 瑞典皇家科学院颁发诺贝尔物理学奖。
words.en: The Royal Swedish Academy is a prestigious institution in Sweden, responsible for awarding the Nobel Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, and Economic Sciences, among its other duties.

words.tr: adj. 开创性的；突破性的；
words.ex: This is a groundbreaking discovery in medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这是医学领域的一项开创性发现。
words.en: If something is groundbreaking, it is very new and a big change from other things of its type.

words.tr:
adj. 化学的；
n. 化学品；
words.ex: The lab has a chemical reaction.
words.ex_cn: 实验室里有一个化学反应。
words.en: A chemical is a substance that is used in or produced by a process involving chemistry.

words.ex: The atomic structure of hydrogen is simple.
words.ex_cn: 氢的原子结构很简单。
words.en: relating to atoms or the energy that comes from splitting atoms

words.ex: The doctor used a laser to fix her eye.
words.ex_cn: 医生用激光修复了她的眼睛。
words.en: A laser is a device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.

words.ex: The atom is the smallest part of matter.
words.ex_cn: 原子是物质的最小单位。
words.en: An atom is the smallest unit of ordinary matter that forms a chemical element. Every solid, liquid, gas, and plasma is composed of neutral or ionized atoms.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.ex: Femtochemistry is the study of chemical reactions on very short timescales, typically femtoseconds.
words.ex_cn: 飞秒化学是研究化学反应在极短时间尺度（通常是飞秒）上的学科。
words.en: Femtochemistry is the area of physical chemistry that studies chemical reactions on extremely short timescales, approximately 10^−15 seconds (one femtosecond, hence the name).

words.ex: The swede speaks Swedish and loves meatballs.
words.ex_cn: 这位瑞典人说瑞典语，爱吃肉丸。
words.en: A Swede is a person from Sweden or a type of turnip known as the Swedish turnip.

words.ex: The police started an investigation into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An investigation is a careful search or examination in order to discover facts or information.

words.ex: The old woman predict rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言明天会下雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: He is an alumnus of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的男毕业生。
words.en: An alumnus is a former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.tr: adj. 骚乱的；喧闹的；热烈的
words.ex: The crowd was tumultuous during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人群喧闹不安。
words.en: A tumultuous event or period of time involves many exciting and confusing events or feelings.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The boxing match took place in an arena.
words.ex_cn: 拳击比赛在竞技场举行。
words.en: An arena is a place or scene of activity, debate, or conflict, especially one where a competition or performance is held.

words.tr: phrase. 亚历山大大学（位于埃及亚历山大的一所著名高等教育机构）
words.ex: Alexandria University is one of the oldest educational institutions in Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 亚历山大大学是埃及最古老的教育机构之一。
words.en: Alexandria University is a public research university in Alexandria, Egypt.

words.ex: He was offered a tenure-track position at the university.
words.ex_cn: 他被大学提供了一个终身职位。
words.en: Relating to a teaching position that is intended to lead to a permanent position with tenure.

words.tr: abbr. 哲学博士学位；博士学位；
words.ex: He earned his PhD in physics.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了物理学的哲学博士学位。
words.en: A PhD is the highest academic degree awarded by universities in most countries, representing mastery of a subject area or field of professional practice.

words.tr: 专有名词。宾夕法尼亚大学（美国常春藤盟校之一，位于费城）
words.ex: The University of Pennsylvania is renowned for its business and law programs.
words.ex_cn: 宾夕法尼亚大学以其商业和法律项目而闻名。
words.en: The University of Pennsylvania is a private Ivy League research university located in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.tr: adj. 享有声望的；声望很高的；
words.ex: He got into a prestigious university.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所享有声望的大学。
words.en: A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired because it is considered to be of very high quality.

words.ex: He is doing a postdoctoral research at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他正在哈佛做博士后研究。
words.en: Relating to or denoting research undertaken after completing a PhD.

words.ex: A handful of students stayed after class to ask questions.
words.ex_cn: 少数学生课后留下来提问。
words.en: A handful of something is a small amount of it, especially when it is not enough or when it is difficult to manage.

words.ex: He studies dynamics to understand how forces move objects.
words.ex_cn: 他学习动态学以理解力如何使物体运动。
words.en: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that deals with the motion of bodies under the action of forces, considering the mass and velocity of the bodies.

words.tr: n. 教授的级别（或职位等）
words.ex: He got the professorship at Harvard last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了哈佛大学的教授职位。
words.en: A professorship is the position of a professor in a university or college.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.tr:
n. 踪迹；轨道；小路；跑道；
v. 追踪；跟踪；
words.ex: The dog followed the track of the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 狗跟着兔子的踪迹。
words.en: A track is a path or route along which something moves or travels. It can also refer to marks left by something that has passed, or the act of following such marks to find someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 突破极限；挑战现有边界；超越常规；冒险尝试新事物
words.ex: Scientists are pushing the envelope to discover new space technologies.
words.ex_cn: 科学家们正在突破极限，以发现新的太空技术。
words.en: To attempt to extend the current limits of performance; to innovate, or go beyond commonly accepted boundaries.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.ex: His wisdom helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的智慧帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: Wisdom is the ability to use your knowledge and experience to make good decisions and judgments.

words.tr: phrase. 从……中获益；因……而获得好处
words.ex: He can gain from exercise every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天锻炼都能有所收获。
words.en: to obtain or receive something beneficial from an experience, situation, or activity.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.tr: n. （基督教的）教牧人员；（任一宗教的）牧师; adj. 牧师的，教士的
words.ex: The cleric delivered a powerful sermon.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师发表了一篇有力的布道。
words.en: A cleric is a member of the clergy, especially in the Christian Church.

words.ex: His contribution helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他的贡献帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: A contribution is a gift or payment to a common fund or collection, or the part played by a person or thing in bringing about a result or helping something to advance.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: The travelers found an oasis with water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 旅行者们发现了一个有水和树木的绿洲。
words.en: An oasis is a small area in a desert where water and plants are found, making it a place of relief and beauty in an otherwise barren landscape.

words.tr: n. 灵长类动物学家（primatology 的变形）
words.ex: The primatologist spent years studying the behavior of chimpanzees in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 这位灵长类动物学家花了数年时间研究野生黑猩猩的行为。
words.en: A primatologist is a scientist who studies primates, which include monkeys, apes, and humans.

words.tr: n. 自然环境保护主义者
words.ex: The conservationist protects wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 这位环保主义者保护野生动物。
words.en: A conservationist is someone who works to protect the environment, especially natural resources and wildlife.

words.ex: He gave an arrogant answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: Someone who is arrogant behaves in a proud, unpleasant way towards other people because they believe that they are more important than others.

words.ex: His personality is very friendly and outgoing.
words.ex_cn: 他的个性非常友好和外向。
words.en: The combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.

words.ex: Above all, be kind to others.
words.ex_cn: 最重要的是，对他人要善良。
words.en: Most importantly; especially.

words.ex: He dreamt of flying like a bird.
words.ex_cn: 他梦见自己像鸟一样飞翔。
words.en: To think about something that you would like to happen or achieve.

words.tr:
n. 脏乱；杂乱；
v. 弄糟；
words.ex: The room was a mess after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A mess is a situation that is confused and full of problems, or something that is dirty or untidy.

words.tr: phrase. 弄乱；搞糟；弄得一团糟
words.ex: The children make a mess with their toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们每天都把玩具弄得一团糟。
words.en: To make a mess means to create disorder or confusion by making things untidy or disorganized.

words.tr: phrase. 把…弄得一团糟；搞砸；弄乱
words.ex: He made a mess of his homework and had to start again.
words.ex_cn: 他把作业搞得一团糟，不得不重新开始。
words.en: To handle something in a way that results in a disordered or chaotic state.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.ex: The pollution affected the fish adversely.
words.ex_cn: 污染对鱼类造成了不利影响。
words.en: In a way that prevents success or development; harmfully or unfavorably.

words.ex: He cares about his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他在乎他的朋友们。
words.en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.

words.tr: 短语. 某种；某类；某种类型的
words.ex: He bought some sort of tool to fix the chair.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一种工具来修椅子。
words.en: A phrase used to indicate that something is of a particular type or kind, but without specifying exactly what it is.

words.tr: adj. 西方的；西洋的；西部的；
words.ex: He likes western music and movies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢西方的音乐和电影。
words.en: Western means relating to the countries of the West, especially Europe and America.

words.ex: He knocked out the other player in the boxing match.
words.ex_cn: 他在拳击比赛中击倒了另一名选手。
words.en: To knock someone out means to cause them to become unconscious or to defeat them in a competition.

words.tr: phrase. 认真对待……；严肃看待……
words.ex: You should take your health seriously.
words.ex_cn: 你应该认真对待你的健康。
words.en: To consider something as important and deserving of attention and respect.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.ex: He eats tuna for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃金枪鱼。
words.en: A tuna is a large fish that lives in warm seas and is caught for food.

words.ex: He has a passion for painting.
words.ex_cn: 他对绘画充满激情。
words.en: A very strong feeling of love, hate, anger, enthusiasm, etc.

words.tr: adj. 有抱负的；有志向的； v. “aspire”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is an aspiring writer who dreams of publishing a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有抱负的作家，梦想出版一部小说。
words.en: If you use aspiring to describe someone who is starting a particular career, you mean that they are trying to become successful in it.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: Nelson Mandela was a prominent antiapartheid activist.
words.ex_cn: 纳尔逊·曼德拉是著名的反种族隔离活动家。
words.en: Opposed to the policy of apartheid, especially in South Africa.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr: n. 大胆；莽撞；勇敢；胆量
words.ex: His boldness helped him win the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他的大胆帮助他赢得了比赛。
words.en: The quality of being willing to take risks and act innovatively; confidence or courage in facing danger or difficulty.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: He showed goodwill by helping his neighbor for free.
words.ex_cn: 他通过免费帮助邻居表现出善意。
words.en: A friendly or cooperative attitude or feeling towards others, especially in a business context.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr:
v. 引导；领导；带头；
n. 主导地位；铅；领先；
words.ex: The teacher leads the students to the library.
words.ex_cn: 老师带领学生去图书馆。
words.en: To be in charge of a group, country, or situation; to guide or direct in a course; a position of advantage in a contest or competition; a heavy, malleable, ductile, bluish-white, dense metallic element.

words.ex: He is likely to pass the test.
words.ex_cn: 他很可能通过考试。
words.en: If you say that something is likely to happen or is likely to be true, you mean that it will probably happen or that it is probably true.

words.ex: He was shy during his adolescence.
words.ex_cn: 他在青春期时很害羞。
words.en: Adolescence is the period in a person's life when they develop from a child into an adult.

words.ex: He entered puberty at age 12.
words.ex_cn: 他12岁时进入青春期。
words.en: Puberty is the stage in a person's life when they physically develop from a child into an adult.

words.tr: adj. 长期存在的；经久不衰的
words.ex: They have a long-standing friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着长久的友谊。
words.en: Existing or continuing for a long time.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: He showed his identity card to enter the building.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了身份证以进入大楼。
words.en: Your identity is who you are, or the qualities of a person or group that make them different from others.

words.tr: adj. 青少年的；十来岁的；
words.ex: Teenage boys often like playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 青少年男孩通常喜欢打篮球。
words.en: Teenage is used to describe someone who is between the ages of 13 and 19, or something that is related to or typical of this age group.

words.tr: phrase. 与……发生冲突；与……不协调
words.ex: He will clash with his boss if he refuses to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 如果他拒绝遵守规则，会与老板发生冲突。
words.en: If two people or groups clash with each other, they have a serious disagreement or fight.

words.tr: phrase. 反抗；反叛；抵制；对…不服从
words.ex: The students rebel against unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: To oppose or fight against a government or other authority, often in a violent way.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.tr: adj. 令人费解的；使人困惑的； v. 混淆；“confuse”的现在分词；
words.ex: The instructions are confusing.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明令人费解。
words.en: If something is confusing, it is difficult to understand because it is not clear or is complicated.

words.ex: No matter how tired I am, I finish my homework.
words.ex_cn: 无论我多么累，我都会完成作业。
words.en: used to say that something is not important or does not affect the situation

words.tr: phrase. phr. 在某人手中；由某人掌握；由某人负责
words.ex: The decision is in her hands.
words.ex_cn: 决定权在她手里。
words.en: Under someone's control, care, or responsibility.

words.tr: adj. 失意的；挫败的； v. “frustrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt frustrated when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 当他考试不及格时，他感到失意。
words.en: If you are frustrated, you are upset or angry because you are unable to do anything about a situation.

words.ex: He used to play soccer every day.
words.ex_cn: 他过去每天踢足球。
words.en: If something used to be done or used to be the case, it was done regularly in the past or was the case in the past.

words.ex: He is getting used to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他正在习惯早起。
words.en: To become familiar with something or someone, so that it/they no longer seem(s) new, strange, or difficult.

words.tr: phrase.  进入；干涉；介入；作短时访问
words.ex: He will step in to help when needed.
words.ex_cn: 当需要时，他会介入帮忙。
words.en: To become involved in a situation in order to help deal with a problem.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.ex: He is argumentative in class and always disagrees with the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上爱争辩，总是不同意老师的意见。
words.en: Someone who is argumentative is always ready to disagree or start arguing with other people.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr: phrase. 对…提出要求；对…施加需求；需要…付出（精力、资源等）
words.ex: The job makes high demand on her time.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作对她的时间要求很高。
words.en: To require something from someone or something, often in a way that is challenging or difficult to fulfill.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: He gave an emotional speech about his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于他母亲的感人演讲。
words.en: Something that is emotional is connected with people's feelings. If someone is emotional, they show their feelings very openly, especially because they are upset.

words.tr:
n. 挑战；
v. 提出挑战；
words.ex: Climbing that mountain is a big challenge.
words.ex_cn: 爬那座山是一个巨大的挑战。
words.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.ex: He tries to cope with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To deal effectively with something difficult.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.ex: He is potentially going to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他有可能赢得比赛。
words.en: in a way that is possible or likely to happen or be true

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.tr:
adj. 令人生气的；惹人恼火的
v. 激起；激怒；；“provoke”的现在分词
words.ex: Her comments were deliberately provoking.
words.ex_cn: 她的评论是故意挑衅的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as provoking, you mean that it is likely to make someone react angrily, for example by arguing or fighting.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.ex: You can take the bus, preferably early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 你可以坐公交车，最好是在早上早些时候。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferably to another, you mean that the first thing is more desirable or suitable than the second.

words.ex: This school uses a progressive teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用一种先进的教学方法。
words.en: A progressive person or idea is one that is modern and new, and is interested in change and improvement.

words.tr: adj. 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；
words.ex: He has a muscular arm from lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他因为举重而拥有强壮的手臂。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the muscles; having well-developed muscles.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: The cold water gave her a sudden sensation.
words.ex_cn: 冷水给了她一种突然的感觉。
words.en: A sensation is a physical feeling or a reaction of interest or excitement that something causes in a person or in a group of people.

words.ex: She sits in the garden with serenity.
words.ex_cn: 她坐在花园里，内心平静。
words.en: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.tr: phrase. 需氧量；氧气需求量
words.ex: The patient's oxygen requirement increased due to the severity of the illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于病情严重，患者的氧需要量增加了。
words.en: The amount of oxygen needed for a particular process or organism to function properly.

words.tr: n. 可视化；视觉化；形象化
words.ex: He uses visualization to understand the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用可视化来理解数据。
words.en: Visualization is the process of making something able to be seen or easily imagined.

words.tr: adj. 废弃的；荒芜的；被遗弃的； v. “desert”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The deserted house had broken windows and overgrown grass.
words.ex_cn: 那座废弃的房子有破碎的窗户和茂盛的杂草。
words.en: If a place is deserted, there are no people in it.

words.tr: phrase. 均衡饮食；指摄入各种适量的营养物质，保持营养全面而平衡的饮食方式
words.ex: He eats a balanced diet to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃均衡的饮食来保持健康。
words.en: A balanced diet is a diet that contains the proper proportions of carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, and water necessary to maintain good health.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.tr: n. 紧张；紧张局势；紧张关系；
words.ex: There was tension between the two friends after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 两人争吵后，彼此之间出现了紧张。
words.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. It can also refer to the state of being stretched tight or the degree of tightness of a stretched string, wire, etc.

words.ex: He eats cereal with milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃谷类食品配牛奶。
words.en: A cereal is a grass that is cultivated for the edible components of its grain, composed of the endosperm, germ, and bran.

words.ex: Vegetables are rich in nutrient.
words.ex_cn: 蔬菜富含营养物。
words.en: A nutrient is a substance that is essential for life and growth, such as the vitamins and minerals in food.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.ex: Eating fruits gives you vitamin C.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果可以给你维生素C。
words.en: A vitamin is one of a group of organic substances which are essential in small quantities to the nutrition of most animals and some plants, and which are present in natural foodstuffs or sometimes produced within the body.

words.ex: Rock contains many minerals.
words.ex_cn: 岩石中含有许多矿物。
words.en: A mineral is a solid substance that occurs naturally and has a specific chemical composition and structure.

words.ex: He couldn't hide his frustration after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后无法掩饰自己的沮丧。
words.en: The feeling of being upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 抑制（感情、情绪等）；把……憋在心里
words.ex: He tends to bottle up his feelings instead of talking about them.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于把感情憋在心里，而不是说出来。
words.en: To bottle up means to not allow yourself to show or express strong emotions, such as anger or sadness.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.tr: adj. 被抑制的；幽闭的；被压抑的
words.ex: He felt pent-up anger after the long day.
words.ex_cn: 经过漫长的一天，他感到压抑的愤怒。
words.en: Pent-up emotions or energies are those that someone has not allowed themselves to express or release.

words.tr:
v. 叫喊
n. 喊叫
words.ex: He yells when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时会大喊。
words.en: If you yell, you shout loudly, usually because you are excited, angry, or in pain.

words.tr: phrase. 发泄情绪；宣泄精力；释放压力
words.ex: He runs every day to let off steam.
words.ex_cn: 他每天跑步来发泄情绪。
words.en: If you let off steam, you get rid of your energy, anger, or strong emotions by doing something active or noisy.

words.ex: The toys are in the basement.
words.ex_cn: 玩具在地下室里。
words.en: The basement of a building is a room or area that is partly or completely below ground level.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: I take a shower every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上都洗淋浴。
words.en: A shower is a device that sprays water over you so that you can wash yourself. It is also a short period of rain or snow.

words.ex: The team made a smart strategy to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队制定了一项聪明的策略来赢得比赛。
words.en: A strategy is a plan that you use in order to achieve something.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: The heat is inducing sweating.
words.ex_cn: 热量正在引起出汗。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr: phrase. 集中（精力；注意力等）于
words.ex: He focuses on his homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上专心做作业。
words.en: to direct your attention or effort towards something specific

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.tr:
adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
n. 潜意识；下意识；
words.ex: He made a subconscious decision to help her.
words.ex_cn: 他下意识地决定帮助她。
words.en: The subconscious is the part of your mind that contains feelings and thoughts that you are not directly aware of but that can influence your behavior and emotions.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.ex: He has a migraine every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一都偏头痛。
words.en: A migraine is a severe, often painful headache that can be accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound.

words.ex: The spicy food caused him severe heartburn.
words.ex_cn: 辛辣的食物让他感到严重的胃灼热。
words.en: A burning sensation in the chest, often caused by stomach acid moving up into the esophagus.

words.tr: phrase. 服从；容易遭受；受制于
words.ex: All students are subject to the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 所有学生都必须服从校规。
words.en: Likely to be affected by or to experience something.

words.ex: The prolonged rain caused flooding.
words.ex_cn: 持久的降雨引发了洪水。
words.en: Something that is prolonged continues for a long time, or longer than expected.

words.ex: He permanently moved to Canada last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年永久搬到了加拿大。
words.en: In a way that continues or lasts forever without changing.

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.ex: The manager showed accountability for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理对这个错误承担了责任。
words.en: The fact or condition of being accountable; responsibility.

words.tr: phrase. 肌肉痉挛；肌肉抽搐
words.ex: He experienced a muscle spasm in his back after lifting heavy weights.
words.ex_cn: 他在举重后背部出现了肌肉痉挛。
words.en: A muscle spasm is a sudden, involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles, often causing pain and temporary immobility.

words.tr: adj. 过分活跃的；多动的；亢奋的
words.ex: The hyperactive child runs around the room all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个多动的孩子整天在房间里跑来跑去。
words.en: If someone is hyperactive, they are extremely active and find it difficult to relax or concentrate on one thing for very long.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: Bedwetting is a common issue among young children.
words.ex_cn: 尿床是幼儿中常见的问题。
words.en: The involuntary urination while asleep, especially by children.

words.ex: The child threw a tantrum when he couldn't get what he wanted.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因为得不到想要的东西而发脾气。
words.en: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of anger and frustration, typically in a young child.

words.ex: He has a phobia of spiders.
words.ex_cn: 他有对蜘蛛的恐怖病。
words.en: A phobia is an extreme or irrational fear of or aversion to something.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.ex: He finished his homework before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他在截止日期前完成了作业。
words.en: A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr: adj. 肾脏附近的；肾上腺的
words.ex: The adrenal glands produce hormones that help the body respond to stress.
words.ex_cn: 肾上腺分泌帮助身体应对压力的激素。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a pair of ductless glands situated above the kidneys which secrete adrenaline and other hormones.

words.tr: n. 去甲肾上腺素；降肾上腺素（等于 noradrenalin）
words.ex: Noradrenaline is a neurotransmitter and hormone that plays a key role in the fight-or-flight response.
words.ex_cn: 去甲肾上腺素是一种神经递质和激素，在战斗或逃跑反应中起着关键作用。
words.en: Noradrenaline is a hormone and neurotransmitter that is released by the adrenal glands in response to stress and plays a key role in the body's fight or flight response.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.ex: The doctor examined the patient's salivary glands for any abnormalities.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了患者的唾液腺是否有任何异常。
words.en: A salivary gland is one of the three pairs of glands in the mouth that produce saliva, which is used to moisten food and begin the process of digestion.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.ex: The blood vessel carries blood to the heart.
words.ex_cn: 血管将血液输送到心脏。
words.en: A blood vessel is a tube in the body through which blood flows.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: The patient experienced frequent urination.
words.ex_cn: 患者经历了频繁的排尿。
words.en: The process of excreting urine from the body.

words.ex: He went to the bathroom after breakfast for defecation.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐后去洗手间排便。
words.en: The act of expelling feces from the body.

words.ex: His silence suggested he was unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默暗示他并不开心。
words.en: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: He worked hard to fulfill his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的梦想。
words.en: To fulfill a task, role, or function means to do or perform it as required or expected.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.tr: adj. 具流苏的，具的（等于 fringy）；加穗的；带边饰的
words.ex: The curtains were beautifully fringed with gold thread.
words.ex_cn: 窗帘用金线装饰得非常漂亮。
words.en: Having a decorative border or edging of hanging threads, cords, or strips, typically attached to a garment or material.

words.ex: He became a millionaire after selling his app.
words.ex_cn: 他卖掉自己的应用后成了百万富翁。
words.en: A millionaire is a person whose wealth amounts to a million or more in currency units such as dollars, pounds, or euros.

words.tr: phrase. 花费（金钱、时间等）在……上
words.ex: He spends money on books.
words.ex_cn: 他把钱花在书上。
words.en: To use money, time, or resources for a specific item or activity.

words.ex: They sailed on a yacht during their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们在假期乘游艇航行。
words.en: A yacht is a medium-sized sailboat used for racing or cruising.

words.tr: phrase. v. 留有，剩下；不得不处理（某种情况或感受）
words.ex: After the party, we were left with a lot of cleaning to do.
words.ex_cn: v. 聚会结束后，我们剩下很多清洁工作要做。
words.en: To remain with something or someone after other parts have been removed or used.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr:
adj. 理想的；
n. 理想；典范；
words.ex: This is the ideal place to relax.
words.ex_cn: 这是放松的理想地方。
words.en: An ideal is a principle or value that one actively pursues as a goal, often in the context of ethics or morality.

words.ex: He became famous for his music and gained great fame.
words.ex_cn: 他因音乐而闻名，获得了巨大的名声。
words.en: the state of being known or talked about by many people, especially on account of notable achievements

words.tr: phrase. 达到某人的巅峰；达到个人最高水平
words.ex: The sun reaches its peak at noon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在中午到达最高点。
words.en: To reach the highest point or level of achievement, ability, or performance.

words.tr: 短语动词. 成功开始运营；处于有利地位；生意兴隆
words.ex: Once we get the final approval, we'll be in business.
words.ex_cn: 一旦我们得到最终批准，我们就会开始营业。
words.en: To start operating or functioning, especially in a business context.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.ex: The magnet picks up the iron nail.
words.ex_cn: 磁铁吸起了铁钉。
words.en: A magnet is a piece of iron or other material which attracts iron or steel towards it.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: I recommend this book to you.
words.ex_cn: 我向你推荐这本书。
words.en: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find them good or useful.

words.ex: I occasionally walk my dog in the park.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔在公园遛狗。
words.en: If something happens occasionally, it happens sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.tr: phrase. 特技车手；表演惊险动作的骑手
words.ex: The stunt rider performed a series of breathtaking tricks.
words.ex_cn: 特技骑手表演了一系列令人惊叹的特技。
words.en: A stunt rider is a person who performs daring feats on a motorcycle, often as part of a show or competition.

words.tr: phrase. 有关系；和…连在一起
words.ex: This event is connected with the history of the city.
words.ex_cn: v. 这个事件与城市的历史有联系。
words.en: To be related to or associated with someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.tr: v. 浇铸；使（演员）一再演出同类的角色；给……分配（合乎性格的任务）；视……为原型
words.ex: He was typecast as the villain in every film.
words.ex_cn: 他在每部电影中都被定型为反派角色。
words.en: If an actor is typecast, they are always given the same kind of character to play because they are known for that type of role.

words.tr:
v. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；抨击；达到；
n. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；(演出等)成功；
words.ex: He hit the ball with a bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒打了球。
words.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

words.ex: She felt that it was inappropriate for her to interfere in their personal affairs.
words.ex_cn: 她觉得干预他们的私事是不合适的。
words.en: To involve oneself in a situation where one is not wanted or needed, often causing problems or difficulties.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.ex: They cease to play when it starts to rain.
words.ex_cn: 下雨时他们就停止玩耍。
words.en: If something ceases to exist, it stops existing. If you cease to do something, you stop doing it.

words.ex: She handled the situation expertly.
words.ex_cn: 她熟练地处理了这种情况。
words.en: In a way that shows special skill or knowledge.

words.tr: phrase. 不惜任何代价；无论如何
words.ex: He will finish the project at all costs.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会不惜一切代价完成这个项目。
words.en: If you say that something must be done at all costs, you are emphasizing that it must be done, even if this requires a lot of effort or causes a lot of problems.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.tr:
n. 电影；底片；薄薄的一层；
v. 拍摄电影；
words.ex: I watched a funny film last night.
words.ex_cn: 我昨晚看了一部有趣的电影。
words.en: A film is a series of moving pictures, usually shown in a cinema or on television and often telling a story.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: Watching movies is a popular entertainment.
words.ex_cn: 看电影是一种流行的休闲娱乐。
words.en: Entertainment refers to performances or activities that are intended to amuse or interest an audience.

words.tr: n. 露天历史剧；盛装游行（或庆典）；选美比赛
words.ex: The town held a pageant to show the history of the old kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场露天历史剧，以展示古老王国的历史。
words.en: A pageant is a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes, or an outdoor performance of a historical scene.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.tr: phrase. 大规模地；大范围地
words.ex: They built houses on a large scale after the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 地震后，他们大规模地建造房屋。
words.en: Involving a large number of people or things, or covering a large area.

words.ex: The clear sky was an auspice of good weather.
words.ex_cn: 晴朗的天空是好天气的预兆。
words.en: An auspice is a sign or omen that is believed to predict the future, often seen as favorable or supportive. It can also refer to the protection or support provided by a person or organization.

words.ex: The allocation of funds is decided by the committee.
words.ex_cn: 资金的分配由委员会决定。
words.en: An allocation is an amount of something, especially money, that is given to a particular person or used for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.tr:
n. 山；
v. 逐渐增加；
words.ex: He climbed the mount early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他一大早爬了那座山。
words.en: To mount something means to go up it or to get on it. It can also refer to the act of organizing and beginning something, such as an event or an exhibition.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.ex: He did not adequately prepare for the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有充分准备考试。
words.en: To an adequate degree; sufficiently.

words.ex: The cake has a sweet flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有一种甜味。
words.en: The flavor of a food or drink is its taste, especially a pleasant or distinctive one.

words.ex: They celebrated their wedding anniversary with dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们用晚餐庆祝结婚纪念日。
words.en: An anniversary is a date which is remembered or celebrated because a special event happened on that date in a previous year.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: This plan is workable and cheap.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且便宜。
words.en: If something is workable, it can be done, used, or put into operation successfully.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的；一流的；处于领导地位的； v. “lead”的现在分词；带领；领导；
words.ex: He is the leading scientist in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的科学家。
words.en: If something is leading in a particular area, it is the most important or advanced thing in that area.

words.ex: The crowd was massed at the entrance, waiting for the doors to open.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集在入口处，等待着大门的开启。
words.en: Gathered or assembled in large numbers or quantities.

words.ex: Bear in mind that the bus leaves at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 请记住，公交车晚上6点发车。
words.en: If you tell someone to bear something in mind, you are reminding or warning them about something important which they should remember.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.tr: phrase. 受支配；从属于；受制；常遭受...
words.ex: He is subject to fines if he breaks the rules.
words.ex_cn: 如果他违反规则，就会被罚款。
words.en: If someone or something is subject to something, especially something bad, it is likely or certain to be affected by it.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.tr: phrase. 意识到；察觉到；知道
words.ex: Be aware of the danger near the river.
words.ex_cn: 注意河边的危险。
words.en: To have knowledge or understanding of something.

words.ex: She responded theatrically to the news.
words.ex_cn: 她戏剧化地对这则新闻做出了反应。
words.en: In a manner that is exaggerated and dramatic, often to attract attention or to create an effect.

words.ex: The verdant hills looked beautiful in spring.
words.ex_cn: 青翠的山丘在春天看起来很美。
words.en: Green with grass or other rich vegetation.

words.tr: adj. 庄重的；庄严的；堂皇的；
words.ex: The stately mansion stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 那座庄重的豪宅矗立在山上。
words.en: Something that is stately is impressive because of its size, beauty, or grandeur.

words.tr: v. 使协调一致；使和谐；配上和音
words.ex: The two singers try to harmonize their voices.
words.ex_cn: 两位歌手试图让他们的声音和谐。
words.en: If two or more things harmonize, they combine in a pleasing way, or if you harmonize them, you make them combine in a pleasing way.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.tr:
n. 大头针；
v. 固定；
words.ex: She stuck a pin on the map.
words.ex_cn: 她在地图上别了一枚大头针。
words.en: A pin is a small piece of metal with a sharp point at one end and a round head at the other, used especially for fastening pieces of cloth together.

words.ex: She bought a new garment for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件新衣服。
words.en: A garment is a piece of clothing; used especially in contexts where you are talking about the manufacture or sale of clothes.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.ex: Her courage in facing danger is admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在面对危险时表现出的勇气令人钦佩。
words.en: If you say that something is admirable, you mean that you approve of it or respect it.

words.tr: n.  无袖上衣；束腰外衣
words.ex: She wore a simple tunic over her trousers.
words.ex_cn: 她在裤子上穿了一件简单的紧身上衣。
words.en: A tunic is a loose piece of clothing, usually without sleeves, that reaches to the waist or hips and is worn over other clothes.

words.tr:
n. 天鹅绒；丝绒
adj. 天鹅绒的
words.ex: The chair has a soft velvet cover.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子有柔软的丝绒坐垫。
words.en: A soft fabric with a thick short pile on one side, used for clothing and upholstery.

words.tr: n. 绳绒线；绳绒织物；假绳绒线织物; n. （Chenille）人名；（法）舍尼耶
words.ex: She draped a chenille throw over the back of the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 她在沙发背上披了一条绳绒线毯。
words.en: A soft, tufted cord of silk, cotton, or worsted used in embroidery or for fringing, or a fabric made from this.

words.ex: The new policy substantially improved the results.
words.ex_cn: 新政策实质上改善了结果。
words.en: To a great extent or degree; considerably.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.ex: The two shirts are identical.
words.ex_cn: 这两件衬衫是一样的。
words.en: Exactly the same, or very similar.

words.ex: He made a box from cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 他用纸板做了一个盒子。
words.en: Cardboard is a stiff, heavy paper material that is used for making boxes and other packaging.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: He wears a helmet when he rides a bike.
words.ex_cn: 他骑自行车时戴头盔。
words.en: A helmet is a strong, hard hat which is worn to protect your head.

words.ex: A plume of smoke rose from the chimney.
words.ex_cn: 一股烟从烟囱里升起。
words.en: A plume is a large, soft, feather or a group of feathers, especially one that is used as a decoration.

words.tr:
n. 布帘；垂下的褶皱状
v. 盖上褶缀的布；将（织物）悬挂；懒散地垂着
words.ex: The blue drape covered the window completely.
words.ex_cn: 蓝色的布帘完全遮住了窗户。
words.en: To drape something means to arrange it in a loose, flowing way, especially fabric or clothing.

words.ex: He waved a red banner in the parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在游行中挥舞着一面红旗子。
words.en: A banner is a long strip of cloth with a message or design on it, used especially for advertising or as a symbol of a particular group or cause.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.tr: n. （船上用作信号等的）三角旗；（奖给棒球等联赛优胜队的）锦旗
words.ex: The ship flew a red pennant to signal danger.
words.ex_cn: 那艘船升起一面红色三角旗来警示危险。
words.en: A pennant is a long, narrow, triangular flag that is used as a symbol, especially by ships and sports teams.

words.tr:
n. 花环
v. 给…戴上花环
words.ex: She put a garland on the door for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对在门上挂了一个花环。
words.en: A garland is a circular decoration made from flowers and leaves, which is worn on the head or hung up as a decoration.

words.ex: He bought a new device to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新设备来拍照。
words.en: A device is an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.ex: The temperature remains high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天温度保持很高。
words.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

words.tr: phrase. 追溯到；回溯至（某时间、地点或源头）
words.ex: The origins of this tradition trace back to the 12th century.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源可以追溯到12世纪。
words.en: To find the origin or cause of something by examining the way it has developed or the events that have happened.

words.tr:
adj. 专业的；职业的；
n. 专业人士；
words.ex: He is a professional teacher with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的专业教师。
words.en: A professional is a person who has a job that requires special training and education, especially one that involves a high level of skill or knowledge.

words.ex: This castle dates back to the 12th century.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡可以追溯到12世纪。
words.en: If something dates back to a particular time, it started or was made at that time.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.tr: adj. 可识别的；可辨认的；
words.ex: The stolen bike is identifiable by its red handlebar.
words.ex_cn: 这辆被盗的自行车可以通过它的红色车把识别出来。
words.en: If something or someone is identifiable, they are able to be recognized.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.tr: n. 低声唱歌的人或歌手
words.ex: He was known as a crooner with a soothing voice.
words.ex_cn: 他以声音柔和的低声歌手而闻名。
words.en: A crooner is a singer, especially a man, who sings sentimental songs in a soft, low voice.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

words.ex: The team works in harmony.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队合作得很和谐。
words.en: Harmony is the pleasant combination of different notes of music played at the same time. It can also refer to a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

words.ex: This is a transitional phase between childhood and adulthood.
words.ex_cn: 这是从童年到成年的过渡阶段。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a process or period of transition.

words.tr: phrase. 打碎；分裂；解体；结束；期终放假
words.ex: He broke up the ice with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把冰打碎了。
words.en: To end a relationship or to disintegrate into pieces.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: In the wake of the storm, the city was left in ruins.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，城市变成了一片废墟。
